content:
# Judith Chapter 9 — Disagreement Log
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Summary
**Total Disagreements: 22**
Chapter 9 is Judith's prayer — the most theologically dense and poetically structured passage in the book thus far. Disagreements are concentrated in three areas: (1) the Simeon allusion (vv. 2-4), which has euphemistic language requiring careful handling; (2) the central petition (vv. 7-10), where Judith asks God to sanction her deception; and (3) the closing epithets of vv. 11-12, which form a hymnic list.

---

## Disagreements

**1. v. 1 — opening posture: "fell upon her face"**
- EMET: "fell upon her face"
- LOGOS: "fell upon her face"
- PNEUMA: "threw herself face down on the floor"
- SOPHIA ruling: "fell upon her face" (EMET/LOGOS — Greek *epesen epi prosōpon autēs*)

**2. v. 1 — "uncovered the sackcloth" / "exposed the sackcloth"**
- EMET: "uncovered the sackcloth with which she was clothed"
- LOGOS: "exposed the sackcloth she was wearing"
- PNEUMA: "pulled back her outer garment to bare the sackcloth beneath"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "exposed" is cleaner; PNEUMA adds interpretive detail

**3. v. 1 — "at that very time" / "at that very hour"**
- EMET: "at-that-very-time"
- LOGOS: "at that very hour"
- PNEUMA: "at that same hour"
- SOPHIA ruling: "at that very hour" (LOGOS — *en tō kairō ekeinō* = "in that time/hour")

**4. v. 2 — "loosened the girdle of a virgin"**
- EMET: "who-loosed the-girdle of a-virgin to-defile her"
- LOGOS: "who loosened the girdle of a virgin to defile her"
- PNEUMA: "who stripped a virgin bare"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — the girdle-loosing idiom must be preserved; PNEUMA loses the ritual/euphemistic register of the Greek

**5. v. 2 — "uncovered the thigh to her shame"**
- EMET: "uncovered the-thigh to her-shame"
- LOGOS: "uncovered her thigh to her shame"
- PNEUMA: (collapsed into "stripped a virgin bare")
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — the two-part violation (loosen girdle + uncover thigh) reflects the structure of Gen 34 and must be maintained

**6. v. 2 — "defiled the womb to her reproach"**
- EMET: "defiled the-womb to her-reproach"
- LOGOS: "defiled her womb to her dishonor"
- PNEUMA: (collapsed)
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "dishonor" for *oneidos*; both *aischynē* (shame) and *oneidos* (reproach/dishonor) are preserved separately

**7. v. 3 — "their bed, which was ashamed at their deceit"**
- EMET: "their bed, which was-ashamed at their-deceit, [you gave] to blood"
- LOGOS: "their bed, which was ashamed because of their treachery, you stained with blood"
- PNEUMA: "their bed — fouled by their treachery — you soaked with blood"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "stained with blood" is most measured; preserves the personification of the bed

**8. v. 3 — "struck down slaves together with lords"**
- EMET: "you struck-down slaves-together-with-lords"
- LOGOS: "You struck down slaves along with lords"
- PNEUMA: "You killed the slaves along with their lords"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "along with" is the standard English for *sun*; "killed" (PNEUMA) is blunter than the Greek *epataxas*

**9. v. 4 — "sons beloved of you" / "sons dear to you"**
- EMET: "sons beloved-of-you"
- LOGOS: "sons beloved to you"
- PNEUMA: "sons who love you"
- SOPHIA ruling: "sons who were dear to you" — the Greek *ēgapēmenous hypo sou* = "beloved by you" (passive), not "who love you" (PNEUMA reverses the direction)

**10. v. 4 — "abhorred the pollution of their blood"**
- EMET: "abhorred the-pollution of their-blood"
- LOGOS: "were horrified at the defilement of their own blood"
- PNEUMA: "could not stomach the contamination of their own blood"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "defilement of their own blood" preserves the ritual contamination sense; "stomach" (PNEUMA) is too colloquial

**11. v. 4 — Climactic address: "O God, my God — hear me also: a widow"**
- EMET: "O God, my God, hear me also — a-widow"
- LOGOS: "O God, my God — hear me also: a widow"
- PNEUMA: "O God — my God — listen to me too. I am a widow."
- SOPHIA ruling: "O God, my God — hear me also, a widow" — EMET's appositive structure; "hear" over "listen" for the prayer register

**12. v. 5 — "the things you intended in your mind"**
- EMET: "the things you-intended-in-your-mind have presented-themselves and said, 'Behold, we-are-here'"
- LOGOS: "the purposes you formed in your mind have come forward and said, 'Here we are'"
- PNEUMA: "Your purposes step forward and say: here we are"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS with slight modification — "have stepped forward and said: here we are"

**13. v. 6 — "your judgment is with foreknowledge"**
- EMET: "your judgment is with foreknowledge"
- LOGOS: "your judgment is with foreknowledge"
- PNEUMA: "Your judgment is perfect foreknowledge"
- SOPHIA ruling: EMET/LOGOS — PNEUMA's "perfect" adds an evaluative word not in the Greek

**14. v. 7 — "exalted in horse and rider"**
- EMET: "they are-exalted in horse and rider"
- LOGOS: "they glory in horse and rider"
- PNEUMA: "horses, riders, infantry ranked in columns"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "they glory in horse and rider" renders *hypsōthēsan en hippō kai anabatē* well; PNEUMA adds "ranked in columns" not in text

**15. v. 7 — "who crushes wars" / "who brings wars to nothing"**
- EMET: "the Lord who-crushes wars"
- LOGOS: "the Lord who brings wars to nothing"
- PNEUMA: "the Lord who unmakes armies"
- SOPHIA ruling: **EMET** — "the Lord who crushes wars" — *syntribon polemous* = crushing/shattering wars; "crushes" is the most precise and most striking

**16. v. 8 — "The Lord is your name"**
- EMET: "The-Lord is your-name"
- LOGOS: "The Lord is your name"
- PNEUMA: "That is your name: the Lord"
- SOPHIA ruling: "The Lord is your name" (LOGOS) — the Greek *Kyrios onoma soi* is a formulaic divine address

**17. v. 9 — "what I have planned" / "the thing I have devised"**
- EMET: "what I have-planned"
- LOGOS: "what I have planned"
- PNEUMA: "the plan I have formed"
- SOPHIA ruling: "the plan I have formed" (PNEUMA) — slightly more vivid; the Greek *epinoia mou* = my thought/plan

**18. v. 10 — "beat down with my lips and my deceit"**
- EMET: "beat-down with my-lips and my-deceit the slave-together-with the-ruler"
- LOGOS: "strike down by the deceit of my lips the slave together with his master"
- PNEUMA: "Use the words of my mouth. Use my deception."
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS — "strike down by the deceit of my lips" is the clearest formulation; EMET's word order is awkward; PNEUMA's imperative form is interpretive

**19. v. 11 — Divine epithet series**
- EMET: "a God of-the humble, a-helper of-the-insignificant, a-supporter of-the-weak, a-guardian of-the despairing, a-savior of-the-hopeless"
- LOGOS: "the God of the lowly, the helper of the weak, the upholder of the frail, the protector of the despairing, the savior of those without hope"
- PNEUMA: "the God who bends down to the humble... helper of the small, upholder of the weak, protector of the despairing, savior of those who have no hope left"
- SOPHIA ruling: LOGOS structure with minor adjustments: "the God of the humble, the helper of the lowly, the upholder of the weak, the protector of the despairing, the savior of those without hope"

**20. v. 12 — "Master-of-the-heavens and earth" vs. "Lord of heaven and earth"**
- EMET: "Master-of-the-heavens and earth"
- LOGOS: "Lord of heaven and earth"
- PNEUMA: "Master of heaven and earth"
- SOPHIA ruling: "Lord of heaven and earth" (LOGOS) — *Despota* here is formal address equivalent to "Lord/Master"

**21. v. 13 — "wound and bruise" / "wound and stripe" / "wound and welt"**
- EMET: "a wound and a-bruise"
- LOGOS: "a wound and a stripe"
- PNEUMA: "a wound, a gash, a stripe" (adds "gash" not in text)
- SOPHIA ruling: "a wound and a welt" — *trauma kai mōlōpa*: *mōlōps* = weal/welt from a blow; PNEUMA's tripling is not in the Greek

**22. v. 14 — "guards the race of Israel" / "shields the people of Israel"**
- EMET: "who-guards the-race of Israel except you"
- LOGOS: "who shields the people of Israel but you"
- PNEUMA: "who protects Israel but you"
- SOPHIA ruling: "who guards the race of Israel but you" — EMET's "race" (*genos*) is technically accurate; LOGOS's "shields" is good; SOPHIA blends: "who guards the race of Israel but you"
